translationRepairs: The crown prince's golden carriage was to follow the upper duke's standard of nine as the measure, reduced by one quarter.
For the named items and colors of the emperor's golden carriage, following the upper duke's standard of nine as the measure, one quarter was to be reduced.

s0080's topic is 上用金輅名件色數 (named items and colors of the emperor's golden carriage), reduced by one quarter from the upper-duke standard of nine; the idiomatic wrongly makes the crown prince's carriage the grammatical subject.

Where the sovereign himself trod the ground his carriage reached—unlike mere display pieces—the foot-rest, back-rest, and footway cushions were all of red brocade, while seat cushions, traveling-horse cushions, and three sheer hanging curtains used silver-brown, yellow, and green brocade.

Where the sovereign himself trod the ground his carriage reached—unlike mere display pieces—the foot-rest, back-rest, and footway cushions were all of red brocade, while seat cushions, railing-barrier cushions, and three sheer hanging curtains used silver-brown, yellow, and green brocade.
In s0015, 行馬褥 are cushions for 行馬 (railing barriers/trestles used with carriages), not traveling-horse cushions; the proposed replacement restores the correct sense.

Where the sovereign himself walked in the places his carriage reached—not like other objects that were merely for display—the foot-rest, back-rest, and footway cushions all used red brocade; seat cushions, traveling-horse cushions, and the three sheer hanging curtains used silver-brown, yellow, and green brocade.

Where the sovereign himself walked in the places his carriage reached—not like other objects that were merely for display—the foot-rest, back-rest, and footway cushions all used red brocade; seat cushions, railing-barrier cushions, and the three sheer hanging curtains used silver-brown, yellow, and green brocade.
Same error as the idiomatic field: s0015 行馬褥 denotes cushions for railing barriers/trestles, not traveling horses.
Painted ladder, carrying forks, and traveling horses.
Painted ladder, carrying forks, and railing barriers.
s0050 lists 畫梯、托叉、行馬 as carriage fittings; 行馬 here are railing barriers/trestles, not traveling horses.
Painted ladder, carrying forks, and traveling horses.
Painted ladder, carrying forks, and railing barriers.
Literal s0050 likewise mistranslates 行馬 as traveling horses; railing barriers is the correct ritual sense.

First, the Heavy-Pheasant carriage: green body with gold ornament and gilt-bronze chased floral fittings, twenty-four radiant leaves, one standing gilt phoenix, purple brocade polychrome treasure-floral curtains, green brocade and green oil canopy covers, vermilion silk nets and purple brocade polychrome cloud-dragon belt bands, polychrome gold pheasant-feather side panels, gilt pewter long-shaft phoenix heads, eight standing pheasants on the cross-shaft, incense burner and treasure, propitious-male brocade knots, vermilion-lacquered stool and foot-rest, hand boards and hand fish, red brocade polychrome cushions and linings, green brocade traveling and side curtains, red bamboo curtains with gold edges, gilt-bronze traveling horses, foreign ladder and attendant cushions, footway cushions, hemp ropes in green silk, and oil-cloth wrapping—each in the quantities prescribed.

First, the Heavy-Pheasant carriage: green body with gold ornament and gilt-bronze chased floral fittings, twenty-four radiant leaves, one standing gilt phoenix, purple brocade polychrome treasure-floral curtains, green brocade and green oil canopy covers, vermilion silk nets and purple brocade polychrome cloud-dragon belt bands, polychrome gold pheasant-feather side panels, gilt pewter long-shaft phoenix heads, eight standing pheasants on the cross-shaft, incense burner and treasure, propitious-male brocade knots, vermilion-lacquered stool and foot-rest, hand boards and hand fish, red brocade polychrome cushions and linings, green brocade traveling and side curtains, red bamboo curtains with gold edges, gilt-bronze railing barriers, foreign ladder and attendant cushions, footway cushions, hemp ropes in green silk, and oil-cloth wrapping—each in the quantities prescribed.
s0054's 金塗銅葉段行馬二 are gilt-bronze leaf-segment railing barriers among carriage fittings, not traveling horses.

The first was called the Heavy-Pheasant carriage: green body, gold ornament and gilt-bronze chased floral-leaf segment fittings and nails, twenty-four radiant leaves, one standing gilt phoenix, one purple brocade gold-cut polychrome treasure-floral curtain, one each of green brocade and green oil canopy cover, two each of vermilion silk net and purple brocade polychrome gold-cut cloud-dragon belt bands, two pheasant-feather panels with polychrome gold fittings on both sides, three gilt pewter long-shaft phoenix heads, eight standing pheasants on the cross-shaft, one set of incense burner and incense treasure, knotted with propitious-male brocade bands, one each of vermilion-lacquered stool and foot-rest, one set of hand boards and hand fish, red brocade polychrome gold garment-cushion, one red brocade lining cushion, four green brocade traveling cushions, one green brocade polychrome gold-cut cloud-phoenix side curtain, two red brocade polychrome gold-edged red bamboo curtains, two gilt-bronze leaf-segment traveling horses, one vermilion-lacquered gilt silver-leaf fitted nail foreign ladder, two green brocade foreign-ladder attendant cushions, ten footway cushions, two green silk-wrapped hemp ropes, one oil-cloth wrapping.

The first was called the Heavy-Pheasant carriage: green body, gold ornament and gilt-bronze chased floral-leaf segment fittings and nails, twenty-four radiant leaves, one standing gilt phoenix, one purple brocade gold-cut polychrome treasure-floral curtain, one each of green brocade and green oil canopy cover, two each of vermilion silk net and purple brocade polychrome gold-cut cloud-dragon belt bands, two pheasant-feather panels with polychrome gold fittings on both sides, three gilt pewter long-shaft phoenix heads, eight standing pheasants on the cross-shaft, one set of incense burner and incense treasure, knotted with propitious-male brocade bands, one each of vermilion-lacquered stool and foot-rest, one set of hand boards and hand fish, red brocade polychrome gold garment-cushion, one red brocade lining cushion, four green brocade traveling cushions, one green brocade polychrome gold-cut cloud-phoenix side curtain, two red brocade polychrome gold-edged red bamboo curtains, two gilt-bronze leaf-segment railing barriers, one vermilion-lacquered gilt silver-leaf fitted nail foreign ladder, two green brocade foreign-ladder attendant cushions, ten footway cushions, two green silk-wrapped hemp ropes, one oil-cloth wrapping.
Literal s0054 has the same 行馬 mistranslation; replacing traveling horses with railing barriers matches the Chinese inventory item.

Grand Preceptor, three dukes, princes, and first-rank chief ministers wore large single-stem floral brocade no more than five cun across; chief councillors wore small single-stem floral brocade no more than three cun.

The Three Preceptors, three dukes, princes, and first-rank chief ministers wore large single-stem floral brocade no more than five cun across; chief councillors wore small single-stem floral brocade no more than three cun.
s0225 begins 三師、三公; 三師 are the Three Preceptors as a class, not the Grand Preceptor alone. The proposed 'Three Preceptors' matches the Chinese.
Fifth rank and above wore court dress when hurrying to audience and spread-black boots at the ministry; rain or snow permitted convenience.
Fifth rank and above wore court dress when hurrying to audience and spread black at the ministry; rain or snow permitted convenience.

s0246 赴省則展皁 parallels s0247 展紫 as a dress mode, with no footwear term; 'spread-black boots' is wrong. The proposal correctly removes boots, but the parenthetical '(zhan zao) dress' is awkward; 'spread black' matches the chapter's own rendering of 展紫.
Officials fifth rank and above: hurrying to court then court dress, going to the ministry then spread-black boots; if rain or snow stained clothing they followed convenience.
Officials fifth rank and above: hurrying to court then court dress, going to the ministry then spread black; if rain or snow stained clothing they followed convenience.
Literal likewise invents boots for 展皁; 'spread black' correctly treats it as the dress mode parallel to 展紫.
Hanlin officials, Veritable Record compilers, remonstrance officers, secretaries, and clerks wore rank dress and colored belts at court, narrow purple and gold belt on duty.

Hanlin Academy officials, compilers of the Veritable Record, remonstrance officials, secretaries, and secretarial clerks: when attending court and standing in attendance they wore their rank's dress and colored belt.
s0251 ends at 色帶; 'narrow purple and gold belt on duty' belongs only to the next unit s0252 (當直則窄紫、金帶) and must not be merged into this sentence.
Beside the bands hung pearl-knotted cords half the belt's length—the type Prince Hailing bestowed on Daxing.
Beside the bands hung pearl-knotted cords half the belt's length—the type Prince Hailing bestowed on Daxingguo.
s0279 海陵賜大興國 names the person 大興國 (Daxingguo), not a place 'Daxing'; the proposed personal-name rendering is correct.
Beside the bands pearl knotted cords half the belt length hung down—the kind Prince Hailing bestowed on Daxing State.
Beside the bands pearl knotted cords half the belt length hung down—the kind Prince Hailing bestowed on Daxingguo.
Literal 'Daxing State' wrongly splits 大興國 as a polity; it is Hailing's attendant's personal name, so Daxingguo is required.
